papers.summary: This article explores the dynamics of collaborative and participatory innovations in public health services using Chen et al.’s (2020) typology. Based on a mixed survey of projects awarded under the national “Droits des usagers de la santé” initiative, the study finds that user participation primarily generates operational and capacity-oriented innovations frequently involving external partnerships. However, the study also identifies limitations in citizen engagement, particularly in the evaluation phase of innovations. The article concludes by suggesting avenues for enhancing full co-creation processes in public services to maximize public value.

papers.authors: Pierre Triboulet, Charlène Arnaud, Liz Carey-Libbrecht
papers.summary: The aim of this article is to characterize the modalities of transformative leadership in support of local public action. It posits that this transformation is based on both the democratic and the distributed dimensions of leadership, and that it is concretely manifested in the territory concerned. To operationalize the concept of Territorial Transformative Leadership (TTL), it draws on a case study of a French Region, Occitanie, which is leading the political project to transform production methods from conventional to organic farming (OF). Twenty semi-structured interviews were conducted in Occitanie. papers.summary: Chemical synthesis of certain glycosaminoglycans like hyaluronic acid and chondroitin sulfate has long been challenging due to critical synthetic intermediates lacking in reactivity and inhibiting stereoselectivity. New methodology for the stereoselective formation of 1,2-trans</em>-β glycosidic bonds via catalysis with a hemin</em>-derived iron porphyrin triflate complex has been developed, allowing for the use of hindered secondary glycosyl acceptors and electron deficient glycosyl donors. papers.summary: Apricot (Prunus armeniaca L.) is an economically important fruit crop worldwide with remarkable germplasm diversity, and its fruit quality is primarily determined by key metabolites (e.g., sugars, organic acids, and flavonoids). papers.title: Genome sequence- and annotation-based multilocus sequence typing (MLST) schemes for the fungal pathogen Histoplasma capsulatum
papers.title_ja: 真菌病原体ヒストプラズマ・カプスラーツムのゲノム配列および注釈ベースの多座位配列型（MLST）スキーム
papers.summary: Histoplasma capsulatum is an important fungal pathogen of humans. While genome sequencing has been used for H. capsulatum epidemiology studies, most of these studies are in the form of Illumina reads without an accompanying genome assembly. This limits the development of applications based on genome assemblies, such as genome-based multilocus sequence typing (MLST). Firstly, 403 genome assemblies were generated from Illumina sequencing reads in the SRA/ENA databases. These genome sequences were used to generate MLST schemes with chewBBACA 3.5.4, based on whole genome sequences (wgMLST), NCBI-obtained annotations (annMLST) and annotations obtained with Funannotate 1.8.17 (fanMLST), with 300 and 500 nt minimum ORF length. This archive contains the 6 MLST schemes for chewBBACA 3.5.4, the Prodigal training files and the Supplementary Tables associated with the manuscript submitted.
